You have 20 seconds.
You will hear a teacher giving information about a school trip to a History Museum.

Listen carefully, please, everyone. I've got some information about our trip to the City History Museum tomorrow. We're going there by coach. It'll leave at 8:30, but we'd like everybody to be at school ready to board by 8:15 at the latest, and our coach should arrive as the museum opens at 9:00.
It's not too far away. You'll need some water, but no.
Two other drinks for the journey. You'll be provided with a packed lunch when we get there, but can I remind you that you are not allowed to eat on the coach?

When we arrive, you'll get a questionnaire to do as you go round the exhibitions, which I'll collect from you to check afterwards. The museum will give you a pen too, which you can use, and it'll be a nice souvenir of the day.

The museum has lots of interesting displays to see. My favourite 1 is of an old fashioned street where you can experience the sights, smells and sounds of life 150 years ago. You may even see someone making bread to a traditional recipe. I know you'll love the latest display about how chocolate was made in the city in the past.
Everyone who goes to the museum talks about it.
The museum does have a shop and at the end of the day you can look round it. They have lots of excellent books and a great range of posters. A variety of food can be bought at a snack shop nearby.
If you or your parents would like to find out more about the museum before we visit, you can look at the website www.waysbu RY dot com. Did you get that? Any questions?
